feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is valid. It is iteration 7 (the best raced design, 125.3) with sensor_size raised from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed value. Everything else is unchanged: five sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 and y = 0.03, weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.35, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, last_direction. Nothing is obviously broken.

Evidence: iterations 0 to 8 all ended off_track on every trial, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.068 and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The footprint trend is only partly clean. Iteration 7 (12 mm) beat iteration 6 (8 mm) by 9.5, but it also changed mass, kd and base_speed. Iteration 0 used 12 mm with different gains and scored 26.0, so footprint size has never been isolated with tuned gains beyond that one step. Iteration 8 showed that kp 3.5 with wheel_track 0.11 scored lower (108.4), so neither of those changes should be carried forward.

The main risk is geometry. With 16 mm footprints at 10 mm spacing, neighbouring sensors overlap heavily, so their readings are highly correlated. That can flatten the position-to-signal slope, which lowers the effective steering gain in a way similar to the flatter weight profile in iteration 5. The candidate could therefore hold the line a little longer and still steer less sharply at bends. Watch steering_oscillation and progress, not just line loss.

I am approving rather than revising. The change is one variable, the best-raced base is strong, and a further revision would spend two action runs without new evidence. Iterations are limited (two remain after this one), so the race is the most useful next step.

What to do next depends on the race. If line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer and max_error drops below 0.06 on oval and s-bend, keep the 16 mm footprint and raise base_speed toward 1.5 if oval progress is below about 0.5. If line loss is unchanged or worse than iteration 7 and the score falls, return to sensor_size 0.012 and test base_speed 1.4 as the single next change. If max_error still reaches 0.06 with line loss still occurring, raise kp from 3.0 to 3.5 on its own, with the 12 mm footprint and wheel_track 0.12, since iteration 8's kp change was confounded with the track change.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are 1 or fewer on oval and s-bend but max_error still reaches 0.06, and progress is below about 0.5 on oval, raise base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.5 with the 16 mm footprint held, since iteration 1 at base 1.5 shows the course needs about 1.5 m/s and the candidate's flatter signal may reduce speed-limited progress.

If the score falls below iteration 7 (125.3) with no drop in line_loss_events, revert sensor_size to 0.012 and test base_speed 1.4 alone, because the 16 mm footprints overlap at 10 mm spacing and may flatten the steering slope, as the flatter weights did in iteration 5.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.28 at kd 0.35 while max_error is still near 0.06, lower kp slightly from 3.0 before raising kd, since iteration 6 showed kd 0.45 adding jitter without stopping the excursion.
